newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan to build first sugar refinery.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan to build first sugar refinery.

text.p: A Turkish company is to build a sugar refinery in the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan with a capacity of 45,000 tonnes a year, an Uzbek official said on Tuesday.

Turkey's Turk Sekes Yuksel Isaat, in a joint venture with the republic's state-owned food production company Pishcheprom, is to build the $98 million plant, the first of its kind in the Central Asian republic, a spokeswoman for Pishcheprom said.
Turkey's Eximbank will finance $33 million of the plant, to be built in the town of Druzhba, in the east of the largely desert republic, and to be completed in 1998.
The spokeswoman said there were plans to increase the plant's capacity to 150,000 tonnes per year, based on imports of raw sugar from the Caribbean, mainly Cuba.
Annual sugar consumption in Uzbekistan is around 500,000-600,000 tonnes, she said.
